text: A revenue problem is just a constraint you haven't named yet.

The most expensive number in a business is the one nobody's measuring.

Usually it's the conversion between two stages everyone assumes are fine.

Most owners think it's a lead problem.
Usually it's a follow-up problem.

The symptom is where it hurts. The constraint is where you fix it.

Growth has an order of operations:

1. Find the one constraint limiting everything else
2. Fix it until it's no longer the limit
3. Re-diagnose, the constraint has moved

Most businesses skip step 1 and wonder why effort doesn't turn into growth.

Every company has one constraint that limits everything else.

Right now it's usually one of:
• Retention
• Cash flow
• Sales conversion
• Delivery capacity

Find that one first. Everything downstream gets easier.

Revenue problems are usually symptoms.
Constraints are the disease.

Fastest way to waste a budget:

Scale before you diagnose.

Pricing is the fastest lever you have.

No new leads. No new headcount.
A 10% price increase drops almost straight to margin.

Most businesses are underpriced, because they never actually tested it.

Start trying to leak less.

The retention-first playbook 👇
parts:
Stop trying to grow.

Start trying to leak less.

The retention-first playbook 👇
Acquisition on top of churn is a bucket with holes. You pour faster, it drains faster, you burn cash feeling busy.
Find your leak: where do people go quiet? Signup → first use? First use → habit? Habit → renewal? One of those is bleeding.
Fix onboarding first. People don’t abandon what they’ve actually activated. Get them to the “aha” fast and churn drops on its own.

Then — and only then — scale acquisition. Growth is retention with a smaller leak.

Stop guessing. The System names your #1 constraint and fixes it → www.growthterminal.io/system

you’re moving ten metrics an inch instead of one metric a mile.

The one-metric week 👇
Pick the single number your constraint lives in. Just one. Conversion, or reply rate, or activation — whatever’s lowest.
For 7 days, every action has to move THAT number. If a task doesn’t touch it, it waits.
This kills the real enemy: shallow effort spread across everything. Depth on one lever beats a thin layer on ten.

Next week, new constraint, new metric. That’s a system, not a scramble.
